explanation_en: This adverbial locution literally translates to 'at the first hour' but is universally used to mean 'first thing in the morning' or 'early on.' It is highly common in both professional and casual settings. A common pitfall is trying to translate 'first thing' literally (e.g., 'primera cosa'), which is incorrect in Spanish.

examples.en_text: Tomorrow I have an important meeting first thing in the morning, so I can't be late.
examples.target_text: Mañana tengo una reunión importante a primera hora, así que no puedo llegar tarde.

examples.en_text: The doctor recommended that I get the blood test first thing in the morning and on an empty stomach.
examples.target_text: El médico me recomendó hacerme el análisis de sangre a primera hora y en ayunas.

examples.en_text: I always prefer to travel first thing in the morning to make the most of the day.
examples.target_text: Siempre prefiero viajar a primera hora para aprovechar mejor el día.

examples.en_text: If you send me the email today, I will read it first thing tomorrow morning.
examples.target_text: Si me envías el correo hoy, lo leeré a primera hora mañana.

examples.en_text: We had to go to the supermarket first thing in the morning to avoid the long lines.
examples.target_text: Tuvimos que ir al supermercado a primera hora para evitar las largas colas.

examples.en_text: Students are usually more focused first thing in the morning than in the afternoon.
examples.target_text: Los estudiantes suelen estar más concentrados a primera hora que por la tarde.

explanation_en: This sophisticated expression means to gather, accumulate, or stock up on something, whether physical goods or abstract qualities like strength, patience, or concentration. It is a B2/C1 level formula often found in journalism and literature. Note that it is always followed by the preposition 'de'.

examples.en_text: She decided to speak with her boss, summoning up all her courage.
examples.target_text: Decidió hablar con su jefe, haciendo acopio de todo su valor.

examples.en_text: The neighbors are gathering firewood before winter arrives.
examples.target_text: Los vecinos están haciendo acopio de leña antes de que llegue el invierno.

examples.en_text: The teacher took a deep breath, summoning up patience to explain the topic again.
examples.target_text: El profesor respiró hondo, haciendo acopio de paciencia para explicar el tema otra vez.

examples.en_text: After running ten kilometers, he summoned up his last bit of strength to reach the finish line.
examples.target_text: Después de correr diez kilómetros, hizo acopio de sus últimas fuerzas para llegar a la meta.

examples.en_text: Before the storm, people went to the supermarket, stocking up on water and canned food.
examples.target_text: Antes de la tormenta, la gente fue al supermercado haciendo acopio de agua y comida enlatada.

examples.en_text: I had to summon up serenity to not lose control during the meeting.
examples.target_text: Tuve que hacer acopio de serenidad para no perder el control durante la reunión.

explanation_en: This extremely common idiom means to attract attention, stand out, or be striking. It can also mean to call someone out or reprimand them depending on the context. For advanced learners, mastering its use with indirect object pronouns (e.g., 'me llama la atención' to mean 'it strikes me as curious') is key to sounding natural.

examples.en_text: Her way of dressing always attracted attention in the office.
examples.target_text: Su forma de vestir siempre llamaba la atención en la oficina.

examples.en_text: There was a painting in the living room that caught the eye of all the visitors.
examples.target_text: Había un cuadro en la sala que llamaba la atención de todos los visitantes.

examples.en_text: What caught my attention the most about him was his incredible patience.
examples.target_text: Lo que más me llamaba la atención de él era su increíble paciencia.

examples.en_text: The title of the book caught my eye, so I decided to buy it.
examples.target_text: El título del libro me llamaba la atención, así que decidí comprarlo.

examples.en_text: His constant complaints no longer attracted anyone's attention.
examples.target_text: Sus constantes quejas ya no llamaban la atención de nadie.

examples.en_text: In the middle of the square, a street musician was attracting people's attention.
examples.target_text: En medio de la plaza, un músico callejero llamaba la atención de la gente.

explanation_en: The construction 'una vez' followed directly by a past participle acts as an absolute clause meaning 'once [something has happened].' The participle must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. It is an elegant, native-feeling grammatical shortcut that avoids clunky temporal clauses like 'después de que hayan atravesado'.

examples.en_text: Once we crossed the border, we had to show our passports again.
examples.target_text: Una vez atravesada la frontera, tuvimos que mostrar nuestros pasaportes de nuevo.

examples.en_text: Once you go through the main door, you will see the reception on the left.
examples.target_text: Una vez atravesada la puerta principal, verás la recepción a la izquierda.

examples.en_text: Once we crossed the mountain, the weather became much drier and warmer.
examples.target_text: Una vez atravesada la montaña, el clima se volvió mucho más seco y cálido.

examples.en_text: Once the worst part of the storm was passed, the ship was able to continue its route safely.
examples.target_text: Una vez atravesada la peor parte de la tormenta, el barco pudo continuar su ruta sin peligro.

examples.en_text: Once the economic crisis was overcome, the company began to hire more staff.
examples.target_text: Una vez atravesada la crisis económica, la empresa empezó a contratar a más personal.

examples.en_text: Once he crossed the finish line, the runner collapsed on the ground from exhaustion.
examples.target_text: Una vez atravesada la línea de meta, el corredor se cayó al suelo de cansancio.

explanation_en: While 'girar' or 'doblar' are standard verbs for turning, 'dar la curva' is the idiomatic way to describe navigating or rounding a bend, especially in driving, racing, or running contexts. It sounds highly active and native. Note that 'dar' is used transitively here with 'la curva' as the direct object.

examples.en_text: As soon as we round the bend, we can see the sea and the beach.
examples.target_text: En cuanto damos la curva, podemos ver el mar y la playa.

examples.en_text: The car was going very fast and almost lost control when rounding the bend.
examples.target_text: El coche iba muy rápido y casi pierde el control al dar la curva.

examples.en_text: When we round the bend, you are going to see the hotel entrance on the right.
examples.target_text: Cuando demos la curva, vas a ver la entrada del hotel a la derecha.

examples.en_text: You have to go slowly when turning the corner because there is usually ice in winter.
examples.target_text: Tienes que ir despacio al dar la curva porque suele haber hielo en invierno.

examples.en_text: Yesterday we rounded the bend and came across a truck stopped in the middle of the road.
examples.target_text: Ayer dimos la curva y nos encontramos con un camión parado en mitad de la carretera.

examples.en_text: Cyclists always reduce their speed before rounding the bend.
examples.target_text: Los ciclistas siempre reducen la velocidad antes de dar la curva.

explanation_en: This highly idiomatic expression literally translates to 'filled up to the flag.' It originates from bullfighting and theater registers to describe a venue that is completely sold out or packed with people, but it is now widely used for bars, concerts, and events. It is a fantastic, colorful alternative to simply saying 'muy lleno' or 'abarrotado'.

examples.en_text: The concert hall was packed to the rafters for the opera premiere.
examples.target_text: La sala de conciertos estaba llena hasta la bandera para el estreno de la ópera.

examples.en_text: The football stadium was filled to capacity during Sunday's derby.
examples.target_text: El estadio de fútbol estuvo lleno hasta la bandera durante el derbi del domingo.

examples.en_text: We couldn't have dinner at that restaurant because the terrace was packed to capacity.
examples.target_text: No pudimos cenar en ese restaurante porque la terraza estaba llena hasta la bandera.

examples.en_text: During rush hour, the subway lines are always packed to the rafters.
examples.target_text: En hora punta, las líneas de metro siempre van llenas hasta la bandera.

examples.en_text: The school auditorium was packed to capacity for the talk on technology.
examples.target_text: El salón de actos del colegio estaba lleno hasta la bandera para la charla sobre tecnología.

examples.en_text: In the middle of August, the town's main beach is packed to capacity.
examples.target_text: En pleno mes de agosto, la playa principal del pueblo está llena hasta la bandera.

explanation_en: This phrase means to turn around 180 degrees or turn back. It is more specific than 'darse la vuelta' (which can just mean to turn over or spin around). It is frequently used when someone realizes they cannot proceed and must walk back the way they came.

examples.en_text: When I saw that the shop was already closed, I turned around and went back home.
examples.target_text: Cuando vi que la tienda ya estaba cerrada, me di media vuelta y volví a casa.

examples.en_text: He didn't want to argue anymore, so he turned around and left the room.
examples.target_text: Él no quería discutir más, así que se dio media vuelta y se fue de la habitación.

examples.en_text: If you see that the mountain path is blocked by snow, the best thing to do is turn back.
examples.target_text: Si ves que el camino de la montaña está bloqueado por la nieve, lo mejor es darse media vuelta.

examples.en_text: It started to rain so hard that we turned back halfway through the journey.
examples.target_text: Empezó a llover tan fuerte que nos dimos media vuelta a mitad del trayecto.

examples.en_text: The hikers turned around when they saw the private property sign.
examples.target_text: Los excursionistas se dieron media vuelta cuando vieron el cartel de propiedad privada.

examples.en_text: Don't turn back now that we are so close to reaching the summit.
examples.target_text: No te des media vuelta ahora que estamos tan cerca de llegar a la cima.

explanation_en: This phrase is used to describe an event, moment, or achievement that is so remarkable it will be remembered forever. It is the natural Spanish equivalent of 'to go down in history' or 'to make history.' It is widely used in journalism, sports, and everyday storytelling.

examples.en_text: The goal he scored in the last minute of the match went down in history.
examples.target_text: El gol que metió en el último minuto del partido quedó para la historia.

examples.en_text: That rock concert in the main square went down in the city's history.
examples.target_text: Aquel concierto de rock en la plaza principal quedó para la historia de la ciudad.

examples.en_text: My brother's fall during the wedding went down in family history.
examples.target_text: La caída de mi hermano durante la boda quedó para la historia familiar.

examples.en_text: The president's speech about peace went down in history.
examples.target_text: El discurso del presidente sobre la paz quedó para la historia.

examples.en_text: That winter's snowstorm went down in history because of its strength.
examples.target_text: La tormenta de nieve de aquel invierno quedó para la historia por su fuerza.

examples.en_text: The day we won the national championship went down in the school's history.
examples.target_text: El día que ganamos el campeonato nacional quedó para la historia del colegio.

explanation_en: 'Llevarse [a alguien/algo] por delante' is a very common idiomatic phrasal verb. It means to run over, knock down, or destroy something in one's path, whether physically (like a car hitting a post or a bull knocking down a runner) or metaphorically (like a crisis ruining businesses). It implies a forceful, unstoppable forward motion.

examples.en_text: The driver lost control and has knocked down a traffic sign.
examples.target_text: El conductor perdió el control y se ha llevado por delante una señal de tráfico.

examples.en_text: Last night's heavy storm swept away several trees in the park.
examples.target_text: La fuerte tormenta de anoche se llevó por delante varios árboles del parque.

examples.en_text: Inflation has wiped out many family businesses this year.
examples.target_text: La inflación se ha llevado por delante a muchas empresas familiares este año.

examples.en_text: A distracted truck ran over the highway guardrail.
examples.target_text: Un camión despistado se llevó por delante la valla de seguridad de la autopista.

examples.en_text: The virus has ruined the entire family's vacation plans.
examples.target_text: El virus se ha llevado por delante los planes de vacaciones de toda la familia.

examples.en_text: The new zoning law will destroy this historic neighborhood.
examples.target_text: La nueva ley de urbanismo se llevará por delante este barrio histórico.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'clash of titans,' this expression is used to describe a major confrontation or competition between two powerful entities, such as large corporations, sports teams, or influential figures. It is highly common in journalistic and business registers to dramatize market rivalries. Note that 'choque' comes from the verb 'chocar' (to crash or clash).

examples.en_text: Tomorrow's match between the league's top two teams will be a true clash of titans.
examples.target_text: El partido de mañana entre los dos mejores equipos de la liga será un verdadero choque de titanes.

examples.en_text: The meeting between the directors of both companies was a clash of titans; neither wanted to back down.
examples.target_text: La reunión entre los directores de ambas empresas fue un choque de titanes; ninguno quería ceder.

examples.en_text: The presidential debate turned into a clash of titans when they spoke about the economy.
examples.target_text: El debate presidencial se convirtió en un choque de titanes cuando hablaron de la economía.

examples.en_text: Seeing those two great actors share a scene in the movie was an authentic clash of titans.
examples.target_text: Ver a esos dos grandes actores compartir escena en la película fue un auténtico choque de titanes.

examples.en_text: When my brother and my father argue about politics, it's always a clash of titans because both are very stubborn.
examples.target_text: Cuando mi hermano y mi padre discuten sobre política, siempre es un choque de titanes porque ambos son muy tercos.

examples.en_text: The competition between the two mobile phone brands is a clash of titans that benefits consumers.
examples.target_text: La competencia entre las dos marcas de teléfonos móviles es un choque de titanes que beneficia a los consumidores.

explanation_en: The phrase 'dar un giro' means to take a turn, change direction, or undergo a significant shift. In this context, 'le da un giro' means it changes the dynamic or trajectory of the relationship. It is a very common idiomatic collocation in news and storytelling to describe sudden changes in events.

examples.en_text: Her decision to study abroad completely changes the direction of her career.
examples.target_text: Su decisión de estudiar en el extranjero le da un giro completo a su carrera.

examples.en_text: The end of the movie gave an unexpected twist to the story.
examples.target_text: El final de la película le dio un giro inesperado a la historia.

examples.en_text: We want to hire a new designer to give our brand a new direction.
examples.target_text: Queremos contratar a un nuevo diseñador para darle un giro a nuestra marca.

examples.en_text: The birth of his daughter has turned his life around one hundred and eighty degrees.
examples.target_text: El nacimiento de su hija le ha dado un giro de ciento ochenta grados a su vida.

examples.en_text: This secret spice gives a very special twist to the traditional recipe.
examples.target_text: Esta especia secreta le da un giro muy especial a la receta tradicional.

examples.en_text: A good advertising campaign will give a positive turn to the business.
examples.target_text: Una buena campaña de publicidad le dará un giro positivo al negocio.

explanation_en: A standard financial idiom meaning 'going public' or 'IPO' (Initial Public Offering). Literally 'exit to the stock market,' it is the fixed collocation used in Spanish business news. Avoid translating 'going public' literally as 'ir público,' which is incorrect in Spanish.

examples.en_text: The technology company is preparing its IPO for next year.
examples.target_text: La empresa de tecnología está preparando su salida a bolsa para el próximo año.

examples.en_text: Many investors are waiting for the IPO of that famous restaurant chain.
examples.target_text: Muchos inversores están esperando la salida a bolsa de esa famosa cadena de restaurantes.

examples.en_text: After going public, the founders of the startup became millionaires.
examples.target_text: Tras la salida a bolsa, los fundadores de la startup se convirtieron en millonarios.

examples.en_text: Due to the economic crisis, the company decided to cancel its IPO.
examples.target_text: Debido a la crisis económica, la compañía decidió cancelar su salida a bolsa.

examples.en_text: I think it's a good time to buy shares before they go public.
examples.target_text: Creo que es un buen momento para comprar acciones antes de su salida a bolsa.

examples.en_text: This week's IPO has been the biggest of the last decade.
examples.target_text: La salida a bolsa de esta semana ha sido la más grande de la última década.
